newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia shocked by Bougainville killing.
newsitem.headline: Australia shocked by Bougainville killing.

text.p: Australia expressed shock on Monday at the weekend assassination of the premier of the war-torn Papua New Guinea island of Bougainville and said his death made peace even harder to achieve.
Theodore Miriung, head of the government-backed Bougainville Transitional Government, was shot in front of his family on Saturday evening by at least two gunmen.
A former legal adviser to the secessionist Bougainville Revolutionary Army (BRA), Miriung was appointed head of the transitional government last year.
His task was to negotiate an end to a long-running and bloody rebellion on the island, which is 800 km (500 miles) northeast of the capital Port Moresby.

"The government is shocked and saddened at the reported assassination of Theodore Miriung, premier of the Bougainville Transitional Government," Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said in a statement.
"Miriung was a courageous and influential figure who dedicated himself to the pursuit of a peaceful resolution of the eight-year conflict in Bougainville.
"With his passing this will become all the more difficult to achieve."
The Papua New Guinea government on Sunday also expressed regret at Miriung's death, which Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan said had "hit at the heart and soul of the nation".

Mike Forster, an Australian-based spokesman for the self-styled secessionist Bougainville interim government, said in a statement that it was not impossible that the government itself had been involved.

"Although at this stage it could not be ruled out that elements of the BRA or resistance may be responsible for the assassination, it could also not be ruled out that this was another deliberate attempt by PNG to undermine the will of the Bougainville people to secure their freedom through peaceful means," the statement said.
"Unless PNG allows the international community to mediate in this situation, the peace processes will become irrevocable," Forster said.
